reviews.feedback: Water-flow detail and stone-separation lines were still missing or insufficiently matched to the target.
The water and joint details were present, but the overall proportions, fish-spout sculpt, upper tier, and stone separation treatment still needed closer reference matching.
The flat radial and vertical seam strips touched curved stone only at their centers, leaving visible floating endpoints around the lower and upper basin silhouettes.
Although the seam solids followed the curve, the top faces still read as separate line geometry laid over the stone rather than real block separation.
The basin rim gaps were corrected, but the eight copper finial flute capsules at the very top were still separate surface geometry and visibly floated above the stone.
The flute overlays were removed, but the donut-shaped copper collar exposed its rear half around the narrow finial base, creating a transparent see-through appearance.
The collar must remain a real ring. It should be visible as the camera rotates, with its far arc hidden naturally behind the opaque finial rather than being replaced by a solid disc.
The finial ring was corrected, but the fish heads remained too spherical and nozzle-like compared with the compact sculpted fish masks in the supplied target.
focus: finial triangle winding corrected from inward to outward
opaque front-side depth-tested materials explicitly enforced
browser orbit evidence showing near-arc visibility, far-arc occlusion, and complete top-view concealment
shared custom tapered fish-cranium geometry replaces the spherical head
broad cheeks, compact muzzle, lower jaw, short circular mouth, and dark cavity match the target's mask-like anatomy
side-set eyes, subtle brow ridges, gill plates, fins, and dorsal crest improve the sculpt silhouette
all four water streams begin at their named mouth sockets
browser and optimized Blender close-up evidence confirm the rebuilt fish heads survive export
